stories.title: Gartner: 70% of Enterprises Will Abandon Vendor-Built Agentic AI by 2028
stories.body: Published September 30, 2026, Gartner warned that 70% of enterprises will abandon agentic AI built through vendor forward-deployed engineering (FDE) by 2028, citing soaring costs and an inability to evolve the systems internally. Gartner also flagged a practice it calls 'FDE washing,' where vendors relabel implementation or consulting services as forward-deployed engineering while charging premium fees. A paired forecast adds that fewer than 20% of FDE engagements will convert recurring customer needs into permanent capabilities in the vendor's core product.
stories.why: This is the single most important buying objection a Graas seller will face in 2026: a prospect's CIO has now read Gartner's headline and will ask 'how do we avoid being in that 70%?' Sellers who can articulate how Graas builds internal capability and transfers ownership — rather than creating dependency — have a decisive response to the build-vs-buy stall.

stories.title: Forrester: Build Meaning Before Machines — Why Ontologies and Knowledge Graphs Are Now Core Agentic AI Infrastructure
stories.body: Forrester's blog post argues that when agents lack a governed semantic foundation, they guess at joins, misinterpret metrics, and act on flawed assumptions — making ontologies, semantic layers, and knowledge graphs core architectural requirements, not nice-to-haves. Forrester proposes a layered model: ontologies define knowledge, semantic layers enforce clarity and consistency, and a knowledge graph becomes the long-term 'digital twin' that enables agentic AI to reason and act across the enterprise. Most organizations, Forrester notes, are not yet ready to build a knowledge graph and should start with the semantic layer as the right first step.
stories.why: This is a named Forrester position paper that directly validates the context-layer argument Graas makes on every discovery call — sellers can cite it to reframe the architecture conversation from 'chatbot vendor' to 'data foundation partner.' It also gives sellers language to explain precisely why pilots stall: agents without semantic grounding hallucinate business logic.

stories.title: McKinsey: 'Who Wins When AI Does the Shopping?' — 21,000-Consumer Survey Finds Retailers Are Not Yet Equipped
stories.body: McKinsey's October 28, 2026 Agentic Commerce Consumer Survey, fielded across approximately 21,000 consumers in 11 markets, finds that more than half of global consumers now use AI for shopping tasks, yet its headline conclusion is blunt: companies are not yet equipped to meet the rising demand. McKinsey argues that winning the AI consideration set requires retailers to have AI-ready product information — structured, machine-readable product attributes, real-time inventory feeds, and verified customer feedback that an algorithm can parse directly. The report projects up to $1 trillion in U.S. B2C retail revenue orchestrated through agentic commerce by 2030, with a global figure of $3–5 trillion.
stories.why: This is a named McKinsey report with a specific enterprise readiness finding — the data foundation gap is now a McKinsey-endorsed talking point, not just a vendor claim. Sellers can use it to open conversations with retail heads of e-commerce or digital: 'McKinsey just surveyed 21,000 shoppers and concluded your competitors aren't ready — here is what ready looks like architecturally.'

stories.title: Sierra Reaches $15.8B Valuation on $950M Round; Salesforce Acquires Intercom Fin for ~$3.6B — Agent Vendor Map Redrawn
stories.body: Sierra raised $950 million in May 2026 at a $15.8 billion valuation led by Tiger Global and GV, bringing total funding to approximately $1.6 billion, and separately reported passing $150 million in annual recurring revenue. In a separate move that closed in September 2026, Salesforce acquired Intercom's Fin business for roughly $3.6 billion, folding the $0.99-per-outcome agent into the Salesforce stack. Decagon, the other named rival, reached a $4.5 billion valuation on $250 million raised in January 2026, with ARR growing from $44 million at end-2025 to an estimated $100 million by July 2026.
stories.why: Three of the five named agent vendors Graas competes with or sits beside have changed their capital structure, ownership, or pricing model in the last six months — sellers need to know that Fin is now a Salesforce product, Sierra's $150K floor makes it unsuitable for mid-market retail, and Decagon is growing fast at a lower price point. This reshapes every competitive bake-off conversation.

stories.title: BCG: Agentic AI Boosts CPG In-Stocks 2–4% and Planning Productivity Over 60% in Live Replenishment Deployments
stories.body: A BCG report documents a global CPG leader that redesigned replenishment using GenAI-enabled agents to deliver in-stock alerts and smart DC-to-store transfer recommendations, validated via human-in-the-loop feedback — achieving a 2–4% improvement in in-stock percentage and 40–60% improvement in planning productivity. BCG's supply chain report also cites General Mills, which partnered with Palantir to deploy an AI platform flagging supply chain risks and generating human-validated actions, contributing approximately $14 million in annualized savings. A separate October 26, 2026 press release from C.H. Robinson reports its agents produced more than 80,000 ocean and air freight quotes for over 3,600 customers, cutting quote time from up to three days to two to three minutes and reducing customs processing time by 23%.
stories.why: These are named enterprises with published outcome numbers across replenishment, supply chain risk, and freight — the three workflows where Graas agents are most often positioned. Sellers can walk into a CPG or distributor conversation with specific proof that peers have already moved from pilot to production with measurable P&L impact.
